lesson.explanation: Imagine you type the start of a sentence: The cat sat on the. A language model looks at those words, which is the context it receives, and estimates which words are most likely to come next. It might assign high probability to mat, and lower probability to words like moon or pizza, because those fit the surrounding text less well. Now walk through the steps. First, the model reads the words it has been given. Second, it uses that context to estimate probabilities for possible next tokens, where a token is a word or piece of a word. Third, it picks a likely continuation, such as mat, and adds it to the text. Then the process repeats with the longer text. This is why it is often described as an ultra-smart autocomplete. Notice what this means for you as a prompt writer: the words you provide shape the context, and that context strongly influences what the model predicts. Keep in mind that predicting likely text does not guarantee correct text, so the model can still produce fluent but wrong answers.

questions.prompt: A model completes 'The sky is' with 'blue' most of the time. What is the most accurate explanation?
options: It was told to answer blue and will repeat it exactly
It judged blue to be the true color, as a person would
Blue follows that phrase most often in its training text
It checked a stored fact that the sky is blue

questions.prompt: Why might running the same prompt twice produce different completions?
options: Completions are sampled from probabilities, so lower-ranked words can be picked
The model rethinks its earlier answer and changes its mind
The model rewrites its stored answer each time it is queried
The prompt reaches the model in a slightly different form each run

questions.prompt: A support bot is asked for the refund policy of a company whose documents it never saw, and it writes a convincing policy. What best explains this?
options: It returns the same policy text on every run, so it repeats itself
It continues learned text patterns, so it can invent plausible policy details
It searched the company's policy page and copied the rule
It understood the question and worked out the rule logically
